{{2011–12 Big Ten men's basketball standings}}
The '''2011–12 Michigan Wolverines men's basketball team''' represented the [[University of Michigan]] during the [[2011–12 NCAA Division I men's basketball season]]. The team played its home games in [[Ann Arbor, Michigan]] at [[Crisler Center]] for the 45th consecutive year.<ref name="Michigan Facilities: Crisler Center">{{cite web|url=http://www.mgoblue.com/facilities/crisler-center.html|title=Michigan Facilities: Crisler Center|access-date=November 23, 2013|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131128061819/http://www.mgoblue.com/facilities/crisler-center.html|archive-date=November 28, 2013|url-status=dead}}</ref> It had a [[seating capacity]] of 12,721.<ref name="Michigan Facilities: Crisler Center"/> It was also the team's 95th straight season as a member of the [[Big Ten Conference]]. Fifth-year [[head coach]] [[John Beilein]] led the team, alongside All-Big Ten players [[Trey Burke]], [[Tim Hardaway Jr.]] and [[Zack Novak]]. Burke was named Big Ten Freshman of the Year and was Michigan's first [[Associated Press]] All-American honoree since 1998.

The team's season began with a preseason media day and practices in October 2011.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.umhoops.com/2011/10/12/michigan-basketball-media-day-roundup/|title=Michigan Basketball Media Day Roundup|access-date=October 22, 2011|date=October 12, 2011|publisher=UMHoops.com}}</ref> In February 2012, Michigan hosted [[ESPN]]'s ''[[College GameDay (basketball)|College GameDay]]'' for the first time in a game against [[2011–12 Ohio State Buckeyes men's basketball team|Ohio State]]. It was the eighth time a Big Ten team hosted the show, which began in 2005.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.mgoblue.com/sports/m-baskbl/spec-rel/081111aaa.html|title=ESPN College GameDay Coming to Ann Arbor for Michigan-Ohio State Game|access-date=August 11, 2011|date=August 11, 2011|publisher=[[CBS Interactive]]|work=MGoBlue}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/blog/collegebasketballnation/post/_/id/33942/breaking-down-the-gameday-schedule|title=Breaking down the GameDay schedule|access-date=August 11, 2011|date=August 11, 2011|publisher=[[ESPN]]|author=O'Neil, Dana}}</ref>

The team was in the [[2011–12 NCAA Division I men's basketball rankings|national rankings]] all season and ended as the [[2011–12 Big Ten Conference men's basketball season|2011–12 Big Ten co-champion]] with [[2011-12 Michigan State Spartans men's basketball team|Michigan State]] and [[2011–12 Ohio State Buckeyes men's basketball team|Ohio State]]. It had three victories over teams ranked in the top 10 at the time of the meeting (eighth-ranked [[2011–12 Memphis Tigers men's basketball team|Memphis]], ninth-ranked [[2011–12 Michigan State Spartans men's basketball team|Michigan State]] and sixth-ranked Ohio State). The team was undefeated at home until its last home game of the season. Michigan lost in the semifinals of the [[2012 Big Ten Conference men's basketball tournament|2012 Big Ten Conference tournament]] and bowed out in the second round of the [[2012 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament|2012 NCAA tournament]] to end the season with a 24–10 record. The team won the school's first Big Ten Conference Championship since the [[1985–86 Michigan Wolverines men's basketball team|1985–86 season]] and had the school's best Big Ten record (13–5) since the [[1993–94 Michigan Wolverines men's basketball team|1993–94 season]].

==Roster changes==
The team lost senior captains [[Stu Douglass]] and [[Zack Novak]] as well as senior reserve Corey Person to graduation following the season.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://annarbor.com/sports/um-basketball/grading-the-2011-12-michigan-basketball-seniors-zack-novak-stu-douglass-corey-person/|title=Grading the 2011–12 Michigan basketball seniors: Zack Novak, Stu Douglass, Corey Person|access-date=July 10, 2012|date=March 25, 2012|work=[[AnnArbor.com]]|author=Baumgardner, Nick}}</ref> Person was later granted an extra year of eligibility to return to the team.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://insider.espn.com/blog/colleges/michigan/post/_/id/5351/corey-person-returning-to-michigan-hoops-team|title=Corey Person returning to Michigan hoops|access-date=November 17, 2012|date=July 11, 2012|publisher=[[ESPN]]|author=Rothstein, Michael}}</ref>  At the end of the season, three players ([[Evan Smotrycz]], Carlton Brundidge and Colton Christian) decided to leave the program. Smotrycz, who had started in 42 of the 69 games he played in during his first two years, left the program as the program's fifth all-time three-point shooter with a percentage of 40.5.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/story/_/id/7719072/evan-smotrycz-carlton-brundidge-colton-christian-all-decide-leave-michigan-wolverines|title=Three players leaving Michigan|access-date=March 21, 2012|date=March 21, 2012|publisher=[[ESPN]]|author=Rothstein, Michael}}</ref> Smotrycz transferred to [[Maryland Terrapins men's basketball|Maryland]], Brundidge transferred to [[Detroit Titans men's basketball|Detroit]] and Christian transferred to [[FIU Panthers|Florida International]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.annarbor.com/sports/um-basketball/ex-michigan-guard-carlton-brundidge-will-transfer-to-the-university-of-detroit/|title=Ex-Michigan guard Carlton Brundidge will transfer to University of Detroit|access-date=July 10, 2012|date=June 14, 2012|work=[[AnnArbor.com]]|author=Baumgardner, Nick}}</ref>

Following the season, Trey Burke first said he was not inclined to enter the [[2012 NBA draft]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.freep.com/article/20120317/SPORTS06/120317003/Michigan-s-Trey-Burke-Tim-Hardaway-Jr-not-thinking-about-NBA-prospects-after-loss|title=Michigan's Trey Burke, Tim Hardaway Jr. not thinking about NBA prospects after loss|access-date=March 23, 2012|date=March 17, 2012|work=[[Detroit Free Press]]|author=Snyder, Mark}}</ref> A few days later, however, the realization that the pool of point guards in the 2012 draft was shallow and Burke's stock was high led to some deliberation for him and his family: "When you have a season as a freshman like he did, the NBA, they like them young," Trey's father, Benji Burke said. "They think their ceiling is higher when they're young. Trey had ... a solid season for a freshman. It's going to be one of the weaker point guard drafts in years."<ref name=MTBiaNds>{{cite web|url=https://www.usatoday.com/sports/college/mensbasketball/bigten/story/2012-03-21/trey-burke-nba-michigan/53691584/1|title=Michigan's Trey Burke inquiring about NBA draft status|access-date=March 23, 2012|date=March 21, 2012|work=[[USA Today]]|author=Snyder, Mark}}</ref> Some observers thought Burke was at his peak in terms of NBA potential.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.annarbor.com/sports/um-basketball/michigan-basketball-pg-trey-burke-to-look-into-nba-draft-stock-still-leaning-toward-staying/|title=Michigan basketball PG Trey Burke to look into NBA draft stock, still leaning toward staying|access-date=March 23, 2012|date=March 21, 2012|work=[[AnnArbor.com]]|author=Baumgardner, Nick}}</ref> Eventually, he decided to return to play for Michigan for another year.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/story/_/id/7792387/michigan-wolverines-point-guard-trey-burke-back-2012-13|title=Trey Burke returning to Michigan|access-date=April 9, 2012|date=April 9, 2012|publisher=[[ESPN]]}}</ref>
